topicName: Economic Systems and Government in Business
description: An examination of capitalism, socialism and mixed economies, the basic economic problem of scarcity and choice, and the role of government in regulating and participating in business, with reference to Tanzania's shift from Ujamaa to a market-oriented mixed economy.

mcq.questionText: An economic system is best defined as the way a country:

options.text: Prints and circulates its national currency
Organises the production, distribution and consumption of goods and services
Records imports and exports in the balance of payments

mcq.explanation: An economic system is the framework through which a society decides how to allocate its scarce resources to produce, distribute and consume goods and services.

mcq.questionText: The basic economic problem facing every society arises mainly from:

options.text: Scarcity of resources relative to unlimited wants
High population in urban areas only

mcq.explanation: Human wants are unlimited but the resources to satisfy them are limited (scarce), so every society must make choices about how to use its resources.

mcq.questionText: In a pure capitalist (free market) economy, the main factor that decides what is produced is:

options.text: The price mechanism (forces of demand and supply)

mcq.explanation: In a free market economy resources are allocated by the price mechanism, where the interaction of demand and supply guides producers on what, how and for whom to produce.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a leading feature of a socialist (planned/command) economy?

options.text: Private ownership of all means of production
State ownership and central planning of resources
Profit as the only motive of production
Free entry and exit of firms in every market

mcq.explanation: A socialist or command economy is characterised by state ownership of the means of production and central planning by the government rather than the price mechanism.

mcq.questionText: A mixed economy is one in which:

options.text: Only the government produces all goods
Only private firms operate without any rules
Both the private sector and the public sector take part in economic activities
All trade is conducted through barter

mcq.explanation: In a mixed economy both private enterprise and the government (public sector) participate in production, with the state regulating and complementing the market.

mcq.questionText: Which economic system is most associated with Tanzania today?
mcq.explanation: Since the economic reforms of the mid-1980s Tanzania has operated a market-oriented mixed economy, combining private enterprise with government participation and regulation.

mcq.questionText: The transfer of a government-owned enterprise to private ownership is called:
mcq.explanation: Privatisation is the process of transferring ownership and control of public (state) enterprises to private individuals or firms.

mcq.questionText: The taking over of privately owned businesses by the government is known as:
mcq.explanation: Nationalisation is the acquisition of private firms by the state, placing them under public ownership and control, as happened in Tanzania after the 1967 Arusha Declaration.

mcq.questionText: A business owned and run by the government for the benefit of the public is best described as a:
mcq.explanation: Parastatals or public enterprises are owned and managed by the government, such as TANESCO, to supply essential goods and services.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a way the government participates in or controls business?

options.text: Collecting taxes through the revenue authority
Deciding the private profits each shareholder may keep at home
Providing roads, ports and other infrastructure

mcq.explanation: Government regulates business through licensing, taxation and infrastructure, but it does not dictate how much private profit individual shareholders keep at home.

mcq.questionText: The Arusha Declaration of 1967 led Tanzania to adopt a policy of:

options.text: Complete free trade with no rules

mcq.explanation: The 1967 Arusha Declaration introduced the policy of Ujamaa na Kujitegemea (socialism and self-reliance), under which major means of production were nationalised.

mcq.questionText: Goods such as street lighting, national defence and public roads are referred to as:
mcq.explanation: Public goods are provided by the government because they benefit everyone and the private sector would under-supply them; they are non-excludable and non-rivalrous.

mcq.questionText: A major advantage of the free market (capitalist) economy is that it:

options.text: Guarantees equal income to all citizens
Removes the need for any private property

mcq.explanation: Competition among private firms in a free market drives efficiency, wider consumer choice and innovation as firms strive to attract customers and earn profit.

mcq.questionText: A major disadvantage of a planned (command) economy is that it often leads to:

options.text: Inefficiency, shortages and lack of incentives
Very high private profits for individuals

mcq.explanation: Because central planning lacks the profit incentive and the price signal, command economies tend to suffer from inefficiency, bureaucracy, shortages and poor quality.

mcq.questionText: Which government body is mainly responsible for collecting taxes from businesses in Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: The Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) is the government agency charged with assessing and collecting taxes and duties from businesses and individuals.

fib.questionText: The way a society organises the production and distribution of goods and services to satisfy its wants is called an economic _____.
fib.explanation: An economic system is the structure a country uses to allocate scarce resources among competing uses.

fib.questionText: The economic problem exists because resources are _____ while human wants are unlimited.
fib.explanation: Scarcity of resources relative to unlimited wants forces every society to make choices.

fib.questionText: An economic system in which the means of production are privately owned and resources are allocated by demand and supply is called _____.
fib.explanation: Capitalism, or the free market economy, relies on private ownership and the price mechanism.

fib.questionText: An economy in which the government owns resources and plans the whole economy centrally is called a _____ economy.
fib.explanation: A planned or command economy (socialism) is controlled centrally by the state. 'Command' is also accepted.

fib.questionText: An economy that combines features of both private enterprise and government participation is known as a _____ economy.
fib.explanation: A mixed economy blends the free market with state involvement and regulation.

fib.questionText: The 1967 _____ Declaration introduced the policy of Ujamaa and self-reliance in Tanzania.
fib.explanation: The Arusha Declaration of 1967 set out Tanzania's socialist policy of Ujamaa na Kujitegemea.

fib.questionText: The process of transferring government-owned enterprises into private hands is called _____.
fib.explanation: Privatisation moves ownership of public enterprises to the private sector. 'Privatization' is also accepted.

fib.questionText: Government-owned business organisations such as TANESCO are commonly called public enterprises or _____.
fib.explanation: Parastatals are state-owned enterprises set up to provide goods and services to the public.

fib.questionText: Laws that defend buyers from cheating, dangerous goods and unfair pricing are part of government consumer _____.
fib.explanation: Consumer protection involves government measures, such as standards and fair-trading laws, that safeguard buyers.

fib.questionText: The government body that promotes and protects fair competition among businesses in Tanzania is the Fair _____ Commission.
fib.explanation: The Fair Competition Commission (FCC) enforces competition law and prevents anti-competitive practices in Tanzania.

tf.questionText: Scarcity means that resources are limited compared with people's unlimited wants.
tf.explanation: Scarcity is the gap between limited resources and unlimited human wants, which is the root of the economic problem.

tf.questionText: In a free market economy, all major resources are owned and planned by the government.
tf.explanation: In a free market economy resources are privately owned and allocated by the price mechanism, not by the government.

tf.questionText: A mixed economy allows both private firms and the government to take part in economic activities.
tf.explanation: In a mixed economy both the private and public sectors participate, with the state regulating the market.

tf.questionText: Nationalisation is the transfer of public enterprises into private ownership.
tf.explanation: Nationalisation is the opposite: the government takes over private firms. Transferring public firms to private owners is privatisation.

tf.questionText: Tanzania changed from a socialist (Ujamaa) approach towards a market-oriented mixed economy in the mid-1980s.
tf.explanation: Following economic difficulties, Tanzania adopted liberalisation and privatisation reforms from the mid-1980s, moving to a mixed economy.

tf.questionText: Public goods such as national defence and street lighting are usually provided by private firms for profit.
tf.explanation: Public goods are provided by the government because the private sector would under-supply them since they are non-excludable.

tf.questionText: Issuing business licences is one way the government regulates and controls business activities.
tf.explanation: Licensing allows the government to control who may trade, ensure standards are met and raise revenue.

tf.questionText: A command economy generally provides consumers with a wider variety of goods than a free market economy.
tf.explanation: Command economies tend to offer less choice and suffer shortages, while free markets usually provide greater variety through competition.

tf.questionText: One reason for government intervention in the economy is to provide infrastructure such as roads, ports and electricity.
tf.explanation: Governments build essential infrastructure that supports business but which private firms may not provide adequately on their own.

tf.questionText: Taxation is used by the government both to raise revenue and to influence business behaviour.
tf.explanation: Taxes fund government services and can also be used to discourage harmful activities or protect local industries.

summary.questionText: Define an economic system and state the three central questions every economic system must answer.
summary.correctAnswer: An economic system is the way a society organises the production, distribution and consumption of goods and services to satisfy wants using scarce resources. Every system must answer: what to produce, how to produce, and for whom to produce.
summary.explanation: These three questions arise directly from scarcity and guide how resources are allocated in any economy.

summary.questionText: Explain the basic economic problem and why it forces societies to make choices.
summary.correctAnswer: The basic economic problem is scarcity: resources (land, labour, capital and enterprise) are limited while human wants are unlimited. Because resources cannot satisfy all wants, societies must choose how to use them, and every choice involves giving up the next best alternative (opportunity cost).
summary.explanation: Scarcity and choice are the foundation of economics; opportunity cost measures what is sacrificed when a choice is made.

summary.questionText: State three features of a capitalist (free market) economy.
summary.correctAnswer: Private ownership of the means of production; resource allocation through the price mechanism (demand and supply); the profit motive driving producers; freedom of choice for consumers and producers; and competition among firms.
summary.explanation: These features distinguish capitalism from a state-controlled economy. Any three are acceptable.

summary.questionText: State three features of a socialist (planned/command) economy.
summary.correctAnswer: State ownership of the means of production; central planning by the government; resources allocated according to a national plan rather than prices; emphasis on social welfare and equality rather than private profit; and limited consumer choice.
summary.explanation: A command economy places control of the economy in the hands of the state. Any three are acceptable.

summary.questionText: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of a free market economy.
summary.correctAnswer: Advantages: encourages efficiency and innovation through competition; offers wide consumer choice; rewards hard work through profit. Disadvantages: leads to inequality between rich and poor; may neglect public goods; can result in exploitation of consumers and workers; and may suffer market failure such as monopolies and pollution.
summary.explanation: The free market is efficient but can produce unfair outcomes, which is why governments intervene.

summary.questionText: Explain what a mixed economy is and give two reasons why many countries, including Tanzania, prefer it.
summary.correctAnswer: A mixed economy combines private enterprise with government participation and regulation, so both the private and public sectors operate side by side. Countries prefer it because it gains the efficiency and choice of the market while letting the government correct market failures, provide public goods, reduce inequality and protect consumers.
summary.explanation: The mixed economy balances market efficiency with social fairness, which suits developing economies like Tanzania.

summary.questionText: Describe four ways in which the government participates in and controls business activities.
summary.correctAnswer: Providing public goods and infrastructure (roads, ports, electricity); regulating business through laws, standards and licensing; collecting taxes through bodies such as the TRA; protecting consumers and maintaining fair competition (through the FCC); supporting local industries; and owning public enterprises (parastatals) such as TANESCO.
summary.explanation: Government acts as both a regulator and a participant in the economy. Any four are acceptable.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between the private sector and the public sector, giving one example of each in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: The private sector consists of businesses owned and run by private individuals or firms for profit, for example CRDB Bank or NMB. The public sector consists of organisations owned and controlled by the government to serve the public, for example TANESCO or the Tanzania Ports Authority.
summary.explanation: The two sectors differ in ownership and objectives: private firms seek profit, while public bodies serve the public interest.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between privatisation and nationalisation, with a Tanzanian example of each.
summary.correctAnswer: Privatisation is the transfer of government-owned enterprises to private ownership, such as the privatisation of many parastatals from the 1990s. Nationalisation is the government taking over privately owned firms, as happened to banks and major companies after the 1967 Arusha Declaration.
summary.explanation: The two are opposite processes that reflect shifts between socialist and market-oriented policies in Tanzania.

summary.questionText: Outline how Tanzania's economy changed from the Ujamaa approach to a market-oriented mixed economy, and give two effects of this change.
summary.correctAnswer: After the 1967 Arusha Declaration Tanzania followed Ujamaa (socialism and self-reliance), nationalising major firms and planning the economy. From the mid-1980s, facing shortages and poor performance, it liberalised trade, privatised parastatals and encouraged private and foreign investment, creating a mixed economy. Effects include increased private investment and availability of goods, growth of the private sector, but also greater income inequality and job losses from privatisation.
summary.explanation: The reforms aimed to revive efficiency and growth through the market while keeping a regulatory and welfare role for the state.

hoq.questionText: A Tanzanian sugar factory produces poor-quality sugar at high cost, faces no competitors, and consumers have no alternative supplier. Which combination of government actions would best correct this situation while keeping a mixed-economy approach?

options.text: Nationalise all other factories so the government controls the whole industry
Liberalise the market to allow competing firms to enter and enforce quality standards and fair competition
Ban the sale of sugar entirely to protect consumers
Fix a very high price so the factory earns more profit

hoq.explanation: A mixed-economy solution to monopoly and poor quality is to open the market to competition and use regulation (quality standards and the Fair Competition Commission) rather than to ban the product or monopolise the whole industry.

hoq.questionText: In the 1980s a Tanzanian state-owned firm kept making losses, produced goods of low quality and offered customers little choice, yet workers had no incentive to improve output. Which economic explanation best accounts for these problems?

options.text: Excessive competition forced the firm to overproduce
The absence of the profit motive and price signals reduced efficiency and incentives under central control
Too much private ownership created confusion
Consumers had too many alternative suppliers

hoq.explanation: Under a command system, state firms lack the profit incentive and the guidance of market prices, which typically causes inefficiency, low quality, shortages and weak worker incentives, a key reason Tanzania later liberalised.

hoq.questionText: A government wants private firms to invest in a rural area but no firm will build the road, power line and water supply needed first because they cannot charge users enough to recover the cost. The most appropriate role for the government is to:

options.text: Order the firms to build the infrastructure for free
Provide the infrastructure itself as a public investment to enable private business to follow
Leave the area undeveloped since the market has decided
Raise taxes only on the rural residents to fund themselves

hoq.explanation: Infrastructure such as roads, electricity and water is a public good that private firms under-supply; the government provides it to create conditions in which private investment and business can develop, a core justification for government intervention in a mixed economy.
